items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: we played for King Farouk's wedding

ctx.x: because we are going to be free from England soon and we need people like you to run, to be in high places. So he was happy all the time.

So we stayed there, but we had to leave. It was -- summertime was coming on, we had to go to Holland so Burns and Pastotis were looking at each other and Pastotis was getting eviler every day, so Burns wanted to stay there, but he says, I'll come back. We take off and get our business straight and change -- Egyptian pounds, when you change an Egyptian pound, at the Barclay's Express or the Cook's, you got so much money, and you had gold, and in the meantime we played for King Farouk's wedding. He became the king…

I didn't know that they were Turks but Farouk was a Turk, he wasn't Egyptian and we played for his wedding and I saw all those people and one of them looked like my aunt and she was just happy as she could be, the things that we were doing. In fact, we were the beloved, but Chitteson he almost got put in that thing again. They hesitated to let Chitteson go.
